Say You'll Remember Me #2

Noaptea în care ne-am cunoscut

Abby Jimenez, Alexandru Boțea (Translator)

3.94
394,729 ratings48,723 reviews
Rate this book
Cu o abilitate rară de a scrie povești care îți frâng inima doar pentru a o lipi la loc mai puternică, Abby Jimenez și-a consolidat reputația de maestră a genului romance contemporan.
Câștigătoare a prestigioaselor Goodreads Choice Awards și iubită de o comunitate globală, autoarea revine cu un nou roman care a adunat deja zeci de mii de recenzii de 5 stele și a cucerit topurile internaționale.
Există iubiri așezate și iubiri în numele cărora se poartă războaie – ești gata să pierzi o lume întreagă doar pentru a o păstra pe ea?
Dar ce te faci când realizezi că omul potrivit a fost mereu cu un pas în spatele celui pe care l-ai ales? La scurt timp după acea noapte, Larissa și Mike devin un cuplu. Totuși, pentru Larissa – o tânără hiper-independentă, obișnuită să lupte zilnic pentru supraviețuirea financiară – viața nu devine mai ușoară. Sub fațada de iubit perfect, Mike ascunde o dependență distructivă de alcool, lăsând-o singură exact în momentele în care are cea mai mare nevoie de sprijin.
Aici intervine Chris. Loial până la sacrificiu față de Mike, prietenul său din copilărie, Chris devine din umbră plasa de siguranță a Larissei. O iubește în tăcere și îi demonstrează asta prin gesturi pe care nimeni altcineva nu le face: se trezește cu noaptea în cap să-i deszăpezească mașina, se asigură că nu atinge nici un alergen periculos, o însoțește la spital și o ajută să-și clădească propria afacere. Fără declarații zgomotoase, doar o grijă constantă în momentele în care ea simte că se prăbușește. Între ei se construiește o conexiune atât de profundă, încât spulberă orice promisiune făcută în trecut.
Dar acum apare următoarea problemă: ce ne datorăm nouă vs. ce le datorăm altora?
Chris trăiește o dramă tăcută, sfâșiat între prietenia de-o viață și o atracție imposibil de ignorat. La rândul ei, Larissa trebuie să învețe că iubirea nu ar trebui să fie încă un loc în care trebuie să lupți pentru supraviețuire, ci refugiul tău suprem.
Cu o tensiune care te va face să întorci paginile pe nerăsuflate, Noaptea în care ne-am cunoscut este o dovadă că adevărata chimie nu are nevoie de factor de șoc. Lasă-ți listele de sarcini la ușă, ieși din „modul de supraviețuire” și intră într-o poveste unde ești iubită pentru cine ești, nu pentru problemele pe care le rezolvi pentru cei din jur.

About the author

Abby Jimenez

28 books111k followers
Abby Jimenez is a Food Network winner, #1 New York Times best selling author of Just for the Summer, and recipient of the 2022 Minnesota Book Award for her novel Life's Too Short. Her book Yours Truly was the first romance novel in the history of Book of the Month to win the coveted Dolly Award for Book of the Year. Abby founded Nadia Cakes out of her home kitchen back in 2007. The bakery has since gone on to win numerous Food Network competitions and, like her books, has amassed an international following.

Abby loves a good romance, coffee, doglets, and not leaving the house.

— i am not bashing the author or any fans of this book. please read what you want; this review should not be taken seriously.

ok, this is a full hate review so if you love abby jimenez or this book; PLEASE DON'T READ THIS. you can read whatever you want, so this is never that serious. i will be going through the whole book and there will be spoilers. full‼️SPOILERS‼️in this review. obviously, this is a romance, so there isn't much to spoil. however, i will be going into the details of why this didn't work. my opinion is just that — MY opinion. take everything with a bucket of salt.

for starters, i am so done reading AJ books because it's clear this is not working for me. to put simply, her books don't feel real, at all. nothing about this feels grounded or pragmatic. the only book of hers that i actually enjoyed all the way through was, yours truly — which came out a few years ago. everything after that book that i have read from her ended up being a complete flop and i honestly should have known that this was going to be the same way. for some reason, i had high hopes which i am now regretting a lot. for starters, AJ has a major obsession with medical professionals and tries to include them in every single book of hers. usually, this character is the MMC who has no life but to be a pathetic little shit for our FMC. speaking of — the FMC is usually the most annoying fucking baby ass character you will ever read about who has no life and no long-term goals. because of this dichotomy, the romance between the main characters and never ends up working out. there was a huge list of trigger warnings in the beginning — making the audience, the readers, believe we were in for an emotional journey. color me surprised when everything ended up being severely watered down and very repetitive.

this story essentially follows our two main characters, larissa and chris — who have this weird wrong person-right time entanglement that they keep shoving in the readers face. essentially, way back when, golden boy MD over here was supposed to give a ride to larissa — after this party — and he hesitated because he was not in a great mood. ever since then, she ended up getting into this petty cycle of nothingness and started dating his best friend...which now bring us to the present. mike — the boyfriend/best friend — is the other major presence in this book because there is a huge dynamic that takes place between mike and chris + mike and larissa. for starters, i do not like emotional cheating, especially when both of our main characters are the most annoying insufferable people on planet earth. so, color me surprised when all of this ended up being extremely uncomfortable to read about and the dynamic between the three of them felt like a father and his children.

essentially, our little golden girl, larissa, is a high school dropout and is extremely poor. she apparently lives with her mother who is clinically insane and acts like a fucking child whilst simultaneously using men for their money. good for her, i guess. mike on the other hand, is very clearly struggling with alcoholism and is not checked into this relationship in the slightest, but is trying really hard to make ends meet, even though he is also very financially challenged. lastly, that brings me to chris, who is a really rich and successful pharmacist — who lost his mother to alcoholism. he is stuck in between his best friend and his best friend’s girlfriend playing devil's advocate…i don’t even know what i just typed out because none of this honestly makes any fucking sense. this is literally the entire premise of this book. the very beginning starts off with mike telling chris to be there for larissa for some hospital visit for her mom, and ever since then, both women have just completely leeched onto this man and are practically demanding everything from him. mike on the other hand is clearly struggling, and it seems like nobody around him cares or wants to help him. everyone's real concern is that he’s not a good boyfriend and doesn't coddle a 30-year-old woman and her stupid, shameless mother…

there are several scenes in this book where mike’s so-called friends, are forcing him to take out a literal grown woman out to these fancy ass events with her good for nothing piece of shit mother, just for them to waste hundreds of dollars on the bill...only to never pay. they don’t help. they don’t find a solution. they don’t stop being greedy leeching hoes. they also never put an end to their nonsense. mike is always the one that ends up embarrassed and hurt. while chris, tries really hard to come in and play the martyr by giving the worst fucking advice known to planet earth. the entire damn, us readers know damn well that this man would not care if he wasn’t trying to get in her pants. everything is just for show. whoever said these MDs have this big of a heart outside of work. please, give me a break.

now, i understand not everyone is going to be in the same education or tax bracket as you, but if you know this, i feel like you should have some decorum and either date in your range and shut the fuck up and take what they are willing to give you — or you just need to go marry a rich man and leave everyone else alone. the problem with larissa is she thinks she is so special for not taking another man’s money, but ultimately, the entire book was chris funding her entire life and saving her bitch ass because he felt bad that she was such a pathetic little shit who couldn’t afford anything at the ripe age of 30…there’s absolutely zero logic in this nonsense because her emotional cheating started off because mike was CLEARLY suffering and she wanted to live the high life without doing any work. larissa so obviously was money hungry and wanted a man to provide for her but her superiority complex and ego wouldn’t let her admit it out loud. i have no issues reading about characters that are financially challenged, however, they have to be likable and down to earth. in this case — none of those qualities are present. everybody is just a raging cunt.

there were scenes that where the side characters were forcing mike to take out his girlfriend and his mother to eat at fancy restaurants — even though it was very clear that neither party could afford this. which really brings me to another long list of grievances because why the fuck are his friends inserting in their relationship and why the fuck does she keep going to another man for emotional support, money, and stability??? i also never understood the concept of dragging her mother everywhere with her because how desperate and stupid do you have to be to not tell a 70 year-old woman to just stay at home…? maybe it’s because i’m indian, but my parents don’t just show up anywhere and everywhere where they are not invited. there’s manners and a certain temperament that needs to develop over time, which comes with age, but that is severely lacking in this book.

all the while, these stupid bitches could and should have just broken up and dated the people that they wanted to date. this is the pure definition of causing drama to cause drama because none of this is even necessary or makes any sense in retrospect. everybody in this book acts like a literal fucking child and it genuinely pissed me off reading this because this is not the first time AJ has done this. and every single time this type of tomfoolery took place, chris came in to save the day — dropping hundreds of dollars on that stupid woman and her stupid mother. cue the part where chris is shaming and coming for his best friend. he doesn’t actually sit down and ask him what’s wrong. why he’s struggling. the concern in question was clearly always for that dumbass and her dumbass mom.

the other notable element of this book that made me die laughing out loud, was the absolute whacking that every reader sent AJ’s way last year when she decided to constantly compare her MMC to rhysand. for some reason, she clearly took that personally because in this book this man is on the shorter side — he’s my height — and he’s clearly insecure about his looks and doesn’t think he’s the most attractive one in the bunch…like ok, you are not fooling anybody with this. so, on one hand, we have the dumb FMC who is poor, incompetent, arrogant, and a cheater. and on the other hand, we have the MMC playing superman, rich, not attractive, and also a cheater. what a beautiful couple!

if this book had a theme, it would totally be a guide of how to pity oneself. an entire element of this book was that our main character, larissa, has a severe nut allergy. for some reason, anytime anybody else forgot about that, she acted like the biggest victim on planet earth and chris’ loser ass came to teach everyone a lesson. imagine a PHARMD is threatening you because of someone else's health??? LMFAOOOOO!!! chris was not helping any of the situations they were in because he kept gassing this minute issue up even further, and reprimanding everyone around him — even though this grown ass woman should be able to take care of her own allergies.

this entire book was just a big melodrama soap-opera mess because not one element of this makes any sense given their ages or their professions. i don’t know what kind of fucking doctors AJ is surrounding herself with, but nobody has this much free time to just be running around town with random ass people. there are so many elements of this book where they’re just out here saving animals because of course, animals are more important than human lives...and chris is here just dropping everything at odd hours of the night to go and save her because clearly being 30 years old doesn’t mean anything anymore.

imagine being so daft and dense and screaming and crying to everybody about how you want to be an independent woman, but you don’t even check to ensure whether there are life threatening consequences in your vicinity…even though you have a life-threatening allergy TO A CERTAIN FOOD??!! then to blame every single man in your presence only to get constantly saved by a man…STUPID AS HELL!

“this is the definition of girl math.” derogatory!

fucking fuck off. bye.

I felt so conflicted on this book! On the one hand I LOVE Abby Jimenez’s writing. I think she’s a fantastic writer and created such an amazing complex set of characters, with rich back stories in such a complex situation with each other. I love books that are messy, have morally grey characters, and make you question how you feel about everyone/everything happening.

BUT I feel like Chris and Larissa’s romance got wayyyy over shadowed by the conflict with Mike. I thought I would hate the boyfriends best friend trope but I actually liked the trope! I just wanted the last few chapters to be like the mid point of the book so we could get more time of Chris & Larissa developing their own relationship and processing the fallout and everything that happened.

I’m also excited to get Mikes book next (I may be in the minority on that opinion 😅) idk if I’ll love or hate Mike in book 3 but I know there’s so much to his own story that we don’t yet know.

I love Abby, she’s still one of my favourite romance authors. But unfortunately, this one missed the mark for me!

I was skeptical about the “boyfriend’s best friend” trope going into this, and oddly enough… that didn’t even really bug me while reading this book. But a whole bunch of other things did.

First of all, Chris is an angel. He’s written as the perfect book boyfriend. But he was so good, that it was boring for me to read about, it felt too manufactured, too clean. I honestly found the lengths he was going to serve Larissa essentially right after meeting her was not believable, and really took me out of the immersion of the book. Forcing Mike to pay for her car to be fixed after only dating her for like a month? (Is this something people actually do???) Stuff like that. Everything was too easy for them. It felt dull to read about.

I honestly think this story would have been more impactful if we shifted the timeline. Instead of focusing so much on Chris and Larissa becoming friends, I would have LOVED seeing more of the fallout. The emotional processing that our characters had to do before they could get their HEA. More meaningful interactions with Chris and Mike. Honestly, just more Mike in general. This would have worked great as a triple POV. This felt like a love triangle but one point of the triangle was missing.

I will say, Abby slays a love declaration every time. Fully enjoyed the moment. I loved the last 80 or so pages of this book. I just wanted MORE of this section and less of all the other stuff!

boyfriend’s best friend trope was, uh, quite the risk.

if you loved this book or want to go into this book blind, you probably shouldn’t read my review. proceed at your own risk.

╭──────────.★..─╮
cast of characters
╰─..★.──────────╯

⟡ Larissa the leech = the fmc

⟡ Mike = her mediocre boyfriend

⟡ Chris = Mike’s best friend since childhood & Larissa’s most reliable source of money, support, and pity

╭──────────.★..─╮
tropes & themes
╰─..★.──────────╯

➺ boyfriend’s best friend
➺ poor, high school dropout fmc digging herself out of a hole that her crappy family put her in
➺ stable, acts of service mmc who is a very educated pharmacist, of course
➺ fmc has a nut allergy
➺ alcoholism
➺ loss of a parent
➺ co-owning a dog
➺ forced proximity
➺ strong cast of side characters, per usual

╭──────────.★..─╮
what i enjoyed
╰─..★.──────────╯

➺ Chris was fine. acts of service king or whatever.

╭──────────.★..─╮
what i disliked
╰─..★.──────────╯
(lots of spoilers & specific scenes mentioned below)

✘ normalizing and romanticizing emotional cheating is absolutely absurd to me. quote:

╰› ❝it was funny because i hadn't really seen Chris or Mike in the last two weeks, but it was Chris i was most looking forward to spending time with. i felt a void where that friendship usually was. i didn't realize how big a part of my life he'd become until he wasn't around anymore. and nothing filled that space. not work…or Mom. or Mike.❞

✘ Larissa openly used Mike for her own gain and to better her situation. she admits this without shame, multiple times. quotes:

╰› ❝things with Mike were good, everything was okay. i’d even told him i loved him finally — and i did. it just felt fragile for some reason, like any little thing could change my mind about it.
i was always on the fence with Mike. i was lukewarm about us, all the time.❞
at this point, you have been dating for many months. you are leading him on and USING him when you know he loves you and you do not feel the same. BREAK UP!

╰› ❝if i live with Mike, i won't have to pay rent.
i can finally start making a dent in these bills, get ahead for once, or take an actual day off where i don't have to worry about financially drowning while i'm gone. plus, he's been asking me to. he really wants it—it just makes sense at this point.❞
so you aren’t moving because you LIKE him or because you WANT to? just because it’s a place to go for free. yikes!

✘ the dog (name: Woofarine 🙄) was quirky and a bit cute at first, then it became over the top

✘ Larissa’s mom is a joke. and trashy.

✘ this book felt like 400 pages of a Larissa pity party. she was so set on being an independent woman working herself out of a hole yet ends up relying on men for basically everything? she scoffs at women that would stay home and let their man support them, and yet ends up doing that very thing. bit hypocritical, no?

✘ apparently ignorance is bliss because there is NO WAY any man would be okay with his best friend being that comfortable with his girlfriend. (showing up to her apartment all the time, going to dinners and driving around past midnight together, trading books and having inside jokes, texting constantly, sending selfies with the dog, letting her wear your clothes, shoveling snow off her car without her knowing, letting her cook for you, etc.)

✘ the constant focus on Larissa needing to make an extra $10 just to get by became so stale. you’d think Larissa had a lot more than 24 hours in a day with all the side work she did, and she still got nowhere (until Chris helps her, of course). we get it, she’s broke.

✘ Mike is not the best boyfriend, i’m aware, but the man is clearly depressed and struggling. Larissa couldn’t care less about her own boyfriend, his “migraines”, if he needs mental care, or if he needs any kind of normal(!!!) support from his girlfriend(!!!). she barely even gets to know him over the course of 10-ish months of dating and then leaves him on his own when he is struggling. yikes.

✘ fmc feels “betrayed” when Chris gets a girlfriend. that level of emotional attachment when she is dating his best friend is NOT OKAY. this is her reaction upon meeting Chris’s new girlfriend (she’s still with Mike btw):

╰› ❝this was wrong. everything was wrong. i wanted to fight with someone. i wanted to have a full-blown screaming match. but not with Mike. i wanted to have it with Chris. i wanted to throw things at him, demand an explanation. i wanted an apology, and i couldn't even tell you for what. i was more upset with Chris than i was with my own boyfriend after everything that he did.❞
you’re kidding me, right?

✘ the situations/scenes were so dramatic and unrealistic, it felt ridiculous. (THE DEER PHOBIA, the walk that never ended, Mike pissing himself and the smell never coming out of the carpet, Woofarine killing anything that breathes, and so on.)

✘ Chris gets a girlfriend and literally calls her a “stand in” and admits he’s wasting her time. he says he doesn’t even want to be standing next to her. dude. can we please stop intentionally hurting people? it’s ridiculous. other people shouldn’t be pawns for you to play with in the midst of your yearning.

✘ Mike & Larissa take forever and a day to break up.

✘ the cover is deceptively summery. there isn’t even a scene that matches the cover, really. we start off in the summery months but much of the end of the book is based around Christmas/New Year’s. the story cycles through seasons but doesn’t really scream “summer read”’to me.

╭──────────.★..─╮
the bottom line…
╰─..★.──────────╯

cheating is cheating. whether it’s emotional or physical. EVEN IF the boyfriend is unreliable and not as good of a fit for the fmc. making the boyfriend less desirable from a reader’s standpoint does NOT change the fact that cheating. is. cheating.

╭──────────.★..─╮
notes for readers:
╰─..★.──────────╯

⟡ if you want to know how long it takes for Larissa to dump Mike: 289 pages

⟡ if you want to know how long it takes for Chris & Larissa to have their first kiss: 356 pages

⟡ any spice? no.

I was super excited for this book and really wanted to love it, but it turned out to be a huge disappointment 😞

I’m happy for everyone who loved it and gave it five stars, but for me, this can’t really be considered a romance—it clearly veers into emotional cheating. I didn’t read the summary beforehand; I wanted to go in blind. Honestly, if I had known, I wouldn’t have read it. The love triangle and best friend-girlfriend trope is not something I enjoy—it made me uncomfortable. You can’t be in love with your best friend’s girlfriend.

Larissa was incredibly boring; I didn’t like her at all. I don’t mind her wanting to choose a man who can give her a good life, but it didn’t make her endearing at all. I also felt it was strange that she spent more time with Chris than with her boyfriend Mike. She knew something was going on but didn’t bother asking about it. And I can’t forget her mother—so opportunistic! I absolutely hated her. At the same time, I feel like Mike was naïve, or maybe he trusted his friend too much 😅

Also, I really don’t like the dog 🐶, and I don’t think eating frogs or snakes is anything cute or nice 😬

As for Chris, I really don’t understand what was going through him. His close friend was clearly struggling—what’s the point of friendship if we can’t be there during hard times? I don’t blame Chris alone, but he saw his friend’s actions and instead of helping, he covered for him, making things worse—just so Larissa could be happy. It’s true that we can’t control our feelings, but we can control our actions. The feelings he developed for her happened way too fast and his attention toward Larissa felt a bit over the top, almost as if she wasn’t a grown woman capable of handling herself. Ok, I got over everything, but… what’s with waking up at 4 a.m. to shovel snow off your best friend’s girlfriend’s car? 🥱

The worst part of the book is that Larissa took forever to break up with Mike—10 months! For 77% of the book, I had to endure all the awkwardness and miserable emotions between them.

Honestly, I didn’t care about the ending. It felt like their happiness was built on someone else’s misery. The direction of being in a relationship for 25 years really broke my heart 💔. But now, seeing Abby Jimenez’s announcement about the third book being Mike’s story, I feel relieved.

Overall: Unfortunately, this book was a major letdown for me. Emotional cheating, frustrating characters, and a drawn-out love triangle made it hard to enjoy. I won’t be revisiting this one, but I’m cautiously curious about Mike’s story in the next book. 🐶

Yeah… It’s a NO from me.



This was my first Abby Jimenez book, and I fear I may have started in the trenches because what was this? I’m so confused.

I don’t think I’ve ever read a book so confidently built on emotional cheating. Movies? Yes. I feel like entire cinematic universes thrive on this. But in a book?? Where I have to sit inside everyone’s thoughts?? There’s just something about reading it that makes it even less romantic and more icky.

I don’t mind the boyfriend’s best friend’s trope and I was even hopeful at the beginning after reading Chris and Larissa’s first interactions, but things got awkward really quickly.

I understand relationships are complicated. I understand staying with someone because they’re safe, familiar, and dependable. I understand timing and missed opportunities are a bitchy package. I even understand catching feelings for someone else. Life happens. But. BIG BUT. There comes a point — a very loud, very obvious point — when you start craving someone else’s presence. When you start setting up situations just to see them. When your “friendship” starts feeling a little too emotionally charged. That is your cue to have a moment of self-awareness.



But not Larissa. I think I would’ve appreciated the dynamic more if she had acknowledged what was going on early and done something about it because what do you mean you “don’t know” why the thought of your boyfriend’s best friend sleeping with someone else upsets you?



And why, oh why does she get into a relationship with Mike in the first place? When we meet them at the beginning of the book, they aren’t official yet. She didn’t even have feelings for him, instead she felt a strong connection to Chris. Why not hold off and be sure about how she feels? It seems incoherent to me, and an excuse to force the cheating trope. That’s why I don’t buy it, neither do I empathise with her. The whole dynamic is crazy because she keeps putting herself in situations where she’s constantly comparing the two men. For someone who says she doesn’t want to give up her boyfriend, who hasn’t really done anything wrong (questionable) and might actually be a good man, it just screams self-sabotage to me. And how long does it take to figure it out? I don’t know. But almost 365 days of emotional cheating is a very steep hill to die on. If I had a friend like Larissa, lord knows I wouldn’t be silent because what in the ever-loving nonsense are you doing? Over 10 months?

I know I’m being hard on Larissa, but she had the power to change the course of things. There’s no guarantee that walking away from her boyfriend would have led her to his best friend, but her decisions, and lack of them didn’t exactly make her easy to root for.

Chris on the other hand didn’t even register to me as the MMC. He tried staying away from Larissa at some point, but kept acting like her boyfriend the whole time. Like get your nosy disloyal ass out of someone else's relationship! Then just maybe Mike will mess up fast enough for Larissa to get her head together and leave. I only started to warm up to him at 80% because that's when the romance truly kicked off. Need I say more?

As for Mike, that man was a car crash waiting to happen. Literally, given how many times Chris had to stop him from drunk driving. He’s unreliable, irresponsible, and lies like it’s cardio. I didn’t care for him at all. But even then, I felt a little bad for him because what he needed was AA, not to be strung along like a participation trophy.

And somehow, the biggest victim in all of this is the dog. Because what is a Woofarine? Why is its name Woofarine?

And why is she co-parenting a dog with her boyfriend’s best friend? No matter which way I spin it, it’s still nonsense. Why create that kind of connection with your boyfriend’s best friend in the first place? What kind of boyfriend would even let it slide? In what world is this okay?

This was boring and I fail to see the romance in it. It was just emotionally messy for everyone involved including me the reader.

emotional cheating?? mmm sexy 😍😍 choosing a girl over your childhood best friend? mmm sexy 😍😍 being fucking stupid at the big ol’ age of 30? mmm sexy 😍😍 ignoring the fact that your best friend is an alcoholic even though your only personality trait is that your mother died from excessive alcohol use?? mmm sexy 😍😍

at this point, i don’t think Abby Jiminez’s books are gonna work for me - i’ve only read three, and two of them were under one point seven five stars. the worst part is that i was SO hopeful about her books because she kept being compared to the queen of literary rom coms, Em Hem, but not rightfully so. instead of feeling lush and numerous emotions, i’m filled with rage at the characters and i always come back from reading her books with many less brain cells. the constant romanticisation of cheating (emotional or physical) is really what solidified my distaste for her books. more on that later.

as always, this review will contain ‼️full spoilers‼️ because well, this is a hate review and i have nowhere else to unleash my anger. if you don’t want anything spoiled for this book, please do not read this !!

essentially, this book follows Larissa, a broke high school drop out who, unfortunately, still lives with her deadbeat mom. Larissa works overtime at this cafe while simultaneously balancing being a dog mom and an unfaithful girlfriend. then we got Chris, the boyfriends childhood best friend, and THE most annoying male character ever - like i’m sorry, who the FUCK (??) has a phobia of deer. honestly, even that screams ‼️ RED FLAG ‼️ to me. Larissa and Chris had met a few months ago at a concert, but at that time, Mike (Chris’ best friend) had offered to drive Larissa back to her apartment. Larissa immediately fell head over heels over Mike and they officially got together. flash forward to present day, Mike is now painted as the “toxic alcoholic boyfriend” while Larissa and Chris flirt inappropriately and co - parent a rabid dog. what makes this even funnier is that Chris is described as average looking, and Mike is repeatedly mentioned as “buff” and “athletic” like miss girl really chose the finest one and ran with it……and then regretted it ten months later.

stating the obvious, the emotional cheating in this book made me go CRAZYYYYYYY. choosing the girlfriend of your childhood best friend over him is crazy work. even though Mike was far from being a good boyfriend - getting a dog, going on dates, meeting each others parents, and flirting every five seconds is FAR from appropriate. the worst part is that Larissa doesn’t even break up with Mike until 80 percent through!!!!!!!!!! i’m all for taboo, but all of this unnecessary drama was so easily avoided. Larissa could’ve broken up with Mike numerous times, but yet she didn’t.

i think AJ has a cheating kink - in say you’ll remember me, the father of the FMC has an affair with one of his coworkers, and his family forgives him because apparently their mother dying from terminal cancer was a valid reason to cheat 👹🤡👹🤡👹🤡👹 same thing here, the emotional cheating could’ve been grandly avoided while still making the book “taboo,” just with NO unnecessary and juvenile cheating.

Mike’s alcoholism was brushed over to the point where it felt insensitive. right of the bat, he was introduced as the annoying alcoholic boyfriend - and while, as i mentioned, he was not a stellar boyfriend, Larissa wasn’t even trying to understand him. when she felt that he was distant, she blamed it on his job. when she saw him with one too many drinks, she said it was just to let loose. partners need to pay attention to each other - yet instead of facing Mike face first and confronting him, she ran to Chris and called him a “bad boyfriend.” Chris wasn’t any better. his childhood best friend was an alcoholic - and to top it off, his mother had died from a liver failure caused by alcoholism. he should’ve known. but instead he was too focused on bussing it down with his girlfriend and picking up dead frogs from his dogs mouth 🤡🤡🤡🤡🤡🤡🤡 the way Larissa and Chris dumped Mike because of the peanut butter allergy was the cherry on top - the whole scene was extremely comedic and made me hate both of them a thousand percent more, and mind you, i hated them to begin with. painting Mike out as the villain and adding an SA plot point was extremely callous. #justiceformike.

you can really tell that the author is a millennial because half the things Chris was saying to make Larissa blush was awkward tiktok slang that made me roll my eyes to the back of my brain. the day AJ discovered tiktok, it was the end for us. i HATED how all of the “little things” (such as removing the snow from her car, having an epipen in his bag) that Mike was supposedly doing was actually Chris - it felt so unnecessary.

Chris might be one of my least favourite male characters of all time, and that’s saying something. his complete ignorance to the addiction that his best friend was facing - but at the same time - spending time with his girlfriend and guilt tripping her with money to get with him and to dump her boyfriend was….odd. to at the end, punching his childhood best friend over AN ACCIDENT after Mike admitted his alcoholic tendencies - basically, being the most two faced, self centred, ignorent, annoying, frustrating, idiotic, pick me, i’m not like the other boys MANCHILD i have ever read about in a contemporary romance. like just because you have no game and can’t get pussy, doesn’t mean that you can sabotage someone else’s relationship and paint yourself as the “the perfect boyfriend.”

usually i am not one to be irritated by female main characters, but Larissa was the most hypocritical character i have ever read about. saying that ‘living with your parents at the age of 30’ was childish and showed that you could never commit to a job to YOUR BOYFRIEND whilst still living with your mom and your jerk ass step dad while wholeheartedly balancing 6/7 side jobs is the dumbest shit i’ve ever heard. being pissed at your situationship for having a girlfriend while you’re in a toxic relationship is the type of greed we talk about in the Bible. and the way she reacted to Mike vulnerably admitting his addiction ???? ma’am THAT MAN IS YOUR BOYFRIEND. why are you making it about yourself and your absent druggie father 🤡🤡🤡🤡🤡🤡🤡🤡🤡🤡🤡

the whole situation went like this :
mike : look…i have something to tell you…i’m an alcoholic
larissa: omg no fucking way! he is just like my dad that i haven’t seen in years! and for that reason, i am gonna dump your ass after you just spilled your guts because i’m an annoying ass bitch and i need to stop being so self centred 🤣🤪 i’m soooooo silly!

if by now you can’t understand that BOTH of these main characters are the most juvenile, irritating, exasperating, annoying, maddening, making - you - want - to - jump - off - a - cliff - characters - YOU WILL EVER MEET IN YOUR FUCKING LIFE. i don’t know what to tell ya.

and one final thing, using the word “overstimulation” when the female main character is clearly neurotypical made me bump down a star. because no.

like seriously…how do you make a DOG unlikeable ???

This is probably the most disappointed I’ve ever felt about a book. I’ve been so incredibly excited about this book so when I saw it early in book stores I obviously had to grab it.

I will admit that I hadn’t read the blurb because I like going in blind. But even reading it now, I wouldn’t have expected the book to be what it is.

My main issue with this book is that the main character Larissa is in a relationship with another man for about 80% of this book. In book time it’s about a year. Meanwhile, throughout that entire relationship, she’s also having what you could call a friendship but is much closer to emotionally cheating with his best friend, Chris. For 80 percent of this book you are reading about Larissa being in an honestly quite bad relationship?? For what??

And I’m supposed to find it cute that Chris does what he can to hide Mike’s red flags. He saves him when he’s too drunk to follow up on his plans, helps him pick out gifts for her, throws out everything with nuts when Mike doesn’t do it. But it doesn’t even stop there. He shovels out her car when it’s snowing, he gets an EpiPen and always checks hers when he sees her. He has fucking nightmares about her safety. And the one thing he doesn’t do is warn her about the fact that her boyfriend doesn’t give a shit about her safety?? There’s this whole thing about him being willing to die for her if it means that she’s safe??? Babes this is a contemporary romance, not the time and place for love declarations like that.

Eventually she finally breaks up with Mike and that whole situation is so uncomfortably unsafe for her. Read like such a traumatic event but in the book they just kinda gloss over that part. Then there’s even more drama which was resolved incredibly quickly and easily. If that drama had started at 50%, maybe I would’ve been invested. It could’ve been explored better but not like this?? Truly didn’t give a fuck anymore at that point.

And then there’s this whole down in the dumps fmc thing going on which I’m hating more with every book I read that has this trope. She has bad money issues, she has a million side jobs, she has a shitty family situation, she has a shitty living situation, she has a shitty car. And he? He has money, he has a comfortable job, he has a friend group that’s like family, he has a safe car, he is so obsessed with her that he wants to save her. He buys her food, helps her with her side jobs, and all the crazy shit I mentioned earlier. She ends up losing her job and moving in with him and he motivates her to make a small business out of one of the side jobs she was doing. Which was cute, I will admit. She doesn’t want him to pay so they co-sign a loan, fine. But then he still goes behind her back and buys all this stuff for her small business?? When she’s made it very clear that she doesn’t want to be dependent on another man. He makes her drive his car so she’s safer, he replaces her tires without her knowledge, keeps her favourite things stocked even though he doesn’t use it even before she moves in.

I just hate how the entire book she’s so determined on getting out of her bad situation on her own. And it’s still made clear that she couldn’t have done it without him. If she doesn’t want your help with money, don’t fucking do it behind her back omg.

This is becoming way longer than I intended oops, but there’s still one thing I need to yap about. They rescue a dog together, cute funsies. He can’t take care of it on his own because of his job so she helps him out, all good with me. But every time this fucking dog gets mentioned it’s about him killing animals?? He brings a dead animal inside multiple times. Kills a snake while they’re on a walk. For what?? What was the reason?? It adds absolutely nothing to the plot. The only thing it adds is that he gave her his shirt so she didn’t have to wear hers that got dirty from the snake (and then also carried her backpack and refused sun block cause he didn’t want her hands touching him and causing unholy thoughts like he didn’t have those already). It just pulled me out of the book so much when another dead animal appeared. Just no.

I am really hoping that her next book takes another direction or it might be my last Abby Jimenez book. I love her writing but this plot killed me😭

The Night We Met by Abby Jimenez
Narrated by Teresa Palmer and Zachary Webber
AUDIOBOOK REVIEW:
9 hrs 52 minutes at 1x
6 hrs 35 minutes at 1.5x
About 5 hours at 2x

FORBIDDEN LOVE

Not a subject that everyone will get onboard with-especially when one guy covets his best friend’s girlfriend-but it happens-despite the “Bro code”.

Just ask the Cars who wrote a song about it in 1978 (Best Friend’s Girl)

This is NOT tagged as a ROM-COM

*****

The night that a tight knit group of guys meet Larissa at a concert is just alluded to just a few times. Her car broke down, and she chose to ride home with Mike instead of Chris. She has no money to fix it, and Chris suggests to Mike that he pay for the repairs…

Larissa has fun with Mike but she isn’t 💯 % into him. As she gets to know him-she realizes that he is a good guy at heart but he is also a 30 year old who hasn’t quite grown up yet. He is a licensed Plumber but doesn’t earn his living that way-preferring to be a Personal Trainer-despite a lack of clients and he still drinks like a Frat Boy.

BUT, he did pay for her car repairs-which made them “relationship official” despite those red flags.

Did she feel a sense of obligation after that?

Over several months, we see how Larissa’s relationship with Mike compares with her friendship with Chris.

Whenever Mike doesn’t show up for her-Chris does.

Maybe the guy she DIDN'T ride home with was the better choice for her?

Hindsight is 20-20.

This story unfolds from the alternating POV’s of Chris and Larissa, and just like the first audiobook set in this World, whenever there is a conversation taking place between the two characters, each narrator voices their own character, making the conversations dual narrated and interactive-an audiobook style that I enjoy.

I applaud the author for how she tackled a trope we don’t often see and feel like how Chris and Larissa navigated their growing feelings was handled in a way that allows you to be open to the outcome. They don’t cross the line physically while she is with Mike.

As always, the playful banter worked for me, and I appreciated the CLOSED DOOR this time-appropriate for Larissa who has feelings for two different men over the course of the story.

I did find myself emotionally moved by the ending, which was poignant and bittersweet.

DO READ the author’s notes at the end of what inspired this book-VERY INTERESTING!

AVAILABLE NOW!

Thank You to the Chandler Public Library for the loan of both the written and Audio copies-I always enjoy an immersive reading experience.

🌌 That one night… one choice… that flips everything upside down.
📖 Remember Chris? The pharmacist. The bookworm. The quiet kind of good-looking. The one who seemed like background in a friend group of Instagram models?
💌 Yeah… this is his story now. And it’s about to wreck you.
🐶 He and Larissa are basically co-parenting a chaotic Yorkie.
📚 They trade books, share laughs, and judge bread (pumpernickel supremacy, obviously).and small joys tucked between heartbreaks.
🐾 A slightly feral but ridiculously adorable rescue Yorkie (who owns the story tbh).
🎀 Small problem: he’s her boyfriend’s best friend -A forbidden love—your boyfriend’s best friend kind of forbidden.we go from brother's bsf to bf's bsf very fast lol!
-This cover? Straight-up Wildest Dreams vibes!
👊🏻They both loves reading 🤍 def. Gonna get along!!
🤺 Yearning so heavy you’ll feel it in your bones. The “I want you but I can’t have you” slow burn that’ll eat you alive.
🔥 Longing glances, stolen moments, and the ache of almosts.
✨ All the messy choices life throws at you, wrapped in romance, laughter, and quiet devastation.


Can we just pause for a sec—
because this cover?? this cover is so Dreamy so damn pretty I can't!!- The fireworks, the golden pink sky, the couple sitting by the water with their little Yorkie third-wheeling—it’s giving dreamy, romantic, and heartbreak-in-the-softest-light vibes.—Tell me it’s not “say you’ll remember me, standing in a nice dress, staring at the sunset, babe…”energy. It’s giving romance, longing, nostalgia, and that ache of loving someone you shouldn’t. It’s literally whispering “this is the kind of love that feels like summer but hurts like forever.”

🎯 THE Mood!?
Alexa, play The Night We Met by Lord Huron.. 🎶🌌

It’s sitting under fireworks with someone you can’t have.
It’s laughing until your chest hurts, but crying when no one sees.
It’s love, timing, loyalty, and the ache of what if? wrapped in golden-hour sunsets.


"Buckle up, buttercup – this love story is anything but simple, but it sure is a wild ride!"🌺 Get ready for 300+ pages of "we shouldn’t"… followed by “we did.”

This isn’t just a book—it’s a whole moment.
Pretty cover, devastating premise, Yorkie chaos, forbidden longing…
Abby Jimenez said romance but make it hurt (in the prettiest way possible). 🌸✨

There are just so many things wrong in this book.

Firstly, I am not sure why the author would write such a trope, since it literally screams "cheating". And it was. Abby has been romanticising cheating in this series so much, and it's so disappointing to read since she used to be one of my favourite authors. I have DNF'ed both books in the series so far. Part of Your World is one of my favorite series, and now we get this? BRING THE OLD SERIES BACK

She tried to paint Mike as the bad guy when he was clearly struggling and in desperate need of help. Abby said that Mike will get a "redemption" story in the third book when there is nothing to be redeemed. Yes, he wasn't perfect, but he deserves better than that. Mike is not the problem; he deserves a better friend and girlfriend. The way she wrote his character was so insensitive and uncalled for.

I also can't believe I'm saying this about an Abby MMC, but Chris was a red flag. He was the problem. It doesn't take one to be a man to know that there is a "bro code" you shouldn't mess up. Imagine ruining years of friendship, because you like your friend's girlfriend.

And don't even get me started on the FMC. Abby is incapable of writing likable FMCs. They are all insufferable to me. She is the red flag and just a terrible pick-me person. She made everything about herself and, ugh, I hated it so much. Apparently, she and Mike were still together until the 80% mark? You write a whole ass book for Chris and Larissa just so that they can be a couple at the very end? You write this trope, and they still didn't break up?

Also, some words or phrases were heavily based on TikTok, and I'm like, "Girl, calm down. It doesn't make you cool; it makes you cringe." Can someone ban TikTok for Abby alone?

So far, Abby's books are all the same. TikTok references. Family drama. Shitty FMC.

Giving Abby her flowers for this one because I imagine this would be a very hard book to write. I want to be clear that there was absolutely NO cheating present in this book, but Abby really toed the line as she developed their relationship. The FMC’s character seemed like she was mostly in denial about her feelings while the MMC was actively denying himself for the sake of his friend. It was clear that Chris and Larissa were much more compatible but they both religiously maintained their boundaries, partly to protect Chris and partly so they could continue to be in each other’s lives.

I know the second book wasn’t everyone cup of tea, but I’ve personally loved every book in this series so much! I’ve heard the next book will focus on Chris’s story and I think that might be a challenging book to write as well. I kind of want to punch Chris at the moment so it will be fun to see how Abby flips the script to make me love him. 😆 I have no doubt she’s up for the challenge!

Plot Summary
One small decision after a concert changes everything for Larissa, even if she doesn’t realise it at the time. Now, she’s built a happy, easy life with her boyfriend—sharing routines, inside jokes, and a sense of stability she’s never had before. But there’s one complication: the person she connects with most isn’t her boyfriend, but his best friend, Chris. As their bond quietly deepens, Chris is left torn between his feelings and his loyalty, knowing that acting on them could risk everything.

ᯓ★ 3.75 stars 🎆

While I cannot completely ignore the rampant emotional cheating, I did enjoy this book much better than the book before it. After the disaster that was Say You’ll Remember Me, I was really worried that Abby Jimenez had taken an unfortunate turn that would ruin all her future books for me. While I do think this book is a comeback, it pales in comparison to her older books.

I’ll start with what she did well and what I ultimately enjoyed. As an acts of service girl myself, the appeal of Chris was undeniable. Having someone that thoughtful looking after you and thinking of you even when you’re not there is rather appealing. Do I think that Chris might have been a little excessive with it?? Maybe. Am I mad at it? Definitely not. I also liked how they were both book lovers and dog lovers. And I can’t ignore Abby Jimenez’s charming banter that she always writes into her books.

*Sigh* now let’s get into what absolutely did not work. THE EMOTIONAL CHEATING!! I mean, boyfriend’s best friend. While they’re still dating?!! And in love??!! THATS BOLD. Even for Abby Jimenez. There’s never an excuse for emotional cheating, and the fact that the plot of this book is built on it really bothered me.

Now as AJ’s biggest fan I liked it because I love her writing and I’m so glad that it’s better than her last book. We need the old AJ back!!!!

I want to start this off by saying I spent the entire time picturing jonah hauer king as chris and brec bassinger as larissa—take that information as you will.

admittedly I didn’t like the first book in the series, and I was surprised because I’m usually a huge fan of abby’s books. this book, however, is now one of my favourites.

the night we met puts the slow in slow burn. there’s quiet pining, and they’re friends first. the relationship between chris and larissa is built as friends, which we don’t see a lot of in books nowadays, and I loved it.

I wasn’t sure how it would work with chris being the best friend of larissa’s boyfriend, but it all tied together perfectly.

I won’t go into too much detail because it will spoil the book, but the way abby writes character development is SO special—and this isn’t limited to the main characters and their respective point of view either.

my only wish was that we got more time with chris and larissa as a couple, or perhaps that’s me wanting more time with them in general because I just loved them.

it’s also closed door, so perfect for younger readers or people who want a break from reading spicy books!

I’m looking forward to the next instalment, and I’m hoping it’s about lexi!
